note: Attacker-controlled bytes enter the client fuzzer as the raw input buffer and length.
A TLS client context is created to parse and process the supplied handshake bytes.
The SSL object is allocated and will consume the attacker-controlled BIO stream.
The entire input is copied into the memory BIO, making it the handshake transcript seen by OpenSSL.
OpenSSL parses the attacker-controlled handshake and may reach certificate/key handling paths.
After handshake completion, application-data processing continues on the same attacker-controlled connection state.

Cleanup releases SSL-owned certificate/key structures; the vulnerable path in the target can double-free or use freed DH/EVP_PKEY state during teardown, matching the reported CRYPTO_DOWN_REF -> DH_free -> evp_pkey_free_it crash state.
